information for citizens to secure access to information under the control of public authorities,

IS : 9552 - 1980 

Indian Standard 

SPECIFICATION FOR 

CAMERA USAGE OF 8 mm MOTION-PICTURE 

FILM PERFORATED TYPE S 

0. FOREWORD 

0.1 This Indian Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards 
Institution on 23 July 1980, after the draft finalized by the Cinemato- 
graphic Equipment Sectional Committee had been approved by the 
Electrotechnical Division Council. 

0.2 This standard has been prepared with a view to standardize the 
position of the emulsion, the rate of exposure and also the orientation 
of the area being exposed for 8 mm motion picture film perforated 
Type S. 

0.3 In preparing this standard, assistance has been derived from ISO 
1787-1972 ' Cinematography — Camera usage of 8 mm motion-picture 
film perforated Type S ', issued by the International Organization for 
Standardization ( ISO ). 

0.4 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this 
standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, 
expressing the result of a test, shall be rounded off in accordance with 
IS : 2-1960*. The number of significant places retained in the rounded 
off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this 
standard. 



1. SCOPE 

1.1 This standard specifies the position of the emulsion, the rate of 
exposure and the orientation of the area being exposed for 8 mm motion- 
picture film perforated Type S. 

2. DIMENSIONS AND CHARACTERISTICS 

2.1 The emulsion shall be towards the camera lens, except for special 
processes. 

2.2 The camera speed shall be 18 frames per second for silent use and 
24 frames per second for sound use. This speed corresponds to the pro- 
jection rate specified in IS : 9534-1980f. Other camera speeds may be 
used when special effects are required. 



*Rules for rounding off numerical values ( revised ). 

fSpecification for projector usage of 8 mm Type S motion-picture film for direct 
front projection. 

3 



IS : 9552 - 1980 



2.3 The perforation used for the film positioning device shall be two 
perforations above the perforation adjacent to the image being formed 
when the positioning device is at the bottom of its stroke ( the - 2 posi- 
tion ) ( see Fig. 1 ). This location coincides with the vertical positioning 
device location required for projectors and thereby improves steadiness 
through cancellation. The dimensions of the camera aperture image 
relative to the film positioning are specified in IS : 9577-1980*. 

2.4 In specifying the film positioning device in 2.3, the existence of 
cameras which use other than — * 2 perforations to position the film is 
recognized. Future design, however, is expected to comply with the 
provisions of 2.3.
